reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 (Amendment 1) the compiler must accept FUNCTION SIN written with exactly one argument-1 in parentheses (an identifier, literal or arithmetic expression, §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1) and refuse any other shape: two arguments, an empty list, no list, a reference-modifier on this numeric function (SR2), and (SR4) a SIN reference outside an arithmetic expression.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 edition window sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel / RemovedIn (COBOL1502/COBOL1503); the catalog row carries IntroducedIn 85, so --std 85 admits the function

ConstructRegistry numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: at 85 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE, DISPLAY, ADD operand, PERFORM n TIMES) is COBOL0900 per §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4; inside an arithmetic expression it is not consulted
function-empty-argument-list-2002: at 85 '( )' gets COBOL0900 in addition to the arity COBOL1504

repository-function-2002 picks the remedy text for a keyword-omitted RESERVED intrinsic (LENGTH/SIGN/SUM/RANDOM); SIN is not one, so SIN written without FUNCTION is an undefined data-name at every edition

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 SIN is admitted only inside an arithmetic expression (MOVE/DISPLAY/ADD operand refused, legal at 2023) and an empty '( )' is also an edition error; the one-argument format and its arity refusal are identical

reader.notes: Grammar functionCall admits any argument list; IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore enforces the catalog's MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 (COBOL1504) for every shape, and the SR2 ref-mod and SR4 placement rules are enforced at 85. The 85 path differs from 2023 only where the 85 text is stricter (placement, empty list), each a correct edition arm.
